summary: 1918 60-foot Aermotor LS40 steel fire tower on Gore Mountain, Warren County, New York; blown down 1919, rebuilt 1920; closed to visitors and now a communications site.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

access.note: Closed to visitors; the tower houses communications equipment at the summit of the Gore Mountain Ski Complex.

events.note: Earliest lookout in the sources read: an 18-foot wooden tower established in August 1909
60-foot steel tower; the Register says built, the Conservation Commission 8th Annual Report (listed under 1918) says purchased and erected
Steel tower blown over in a hurricane in October 1919
Acquisition of a 1,861.17-acre parcel in Johnsburg that included the summit observation station (January 11, 1934 item)
Register gives 1988 as the closing year; Wikipedia says fire lookout operations ended at the end of the 1988 season
Officially closed in early 1989, per Wikipedia
Registered December 23, 2022 as US 1701, NY 53; nominated by Laurie Rankin

corrections.why: 5.5 m (18 ft) is the 1909 wooden tower that the 1918 steel tower replaced; the current tower is 60 feet (about 18.3 m) per the Register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says built in 1918; a Conservation Commission annual report listed under 1918 on Forest Lookouts says a 60-foot steel tower was purchased and erected. Both give 1918 for the steel tower.
The Register gives 1988 as the closing year; Wikipedia says fire lookout work ended after the 1988 season and official closure came in early 1989. Both are recorded as events.
US 1701 is this tower's NHLR number (NY 53). A Kentucky tower in the database carries FFLOS US 1701 for a different register, so the shared number is coincidental, not a duplicate.

sources.title: New York State chapter newsletter, January 2020

notes_for_editor: Solid on the 1909 wooden tower, 1918 steel tower, 1919 blowdown and 1920 rebuild (Register, a state report quoted on Forest Lookouts, and the 2020 NYSFFLA newsletter agree). Closure year is disputed: Register says 1988, Wikipedia says lookout work ended after the 1988 season and official closure was early 1989. The record's note that the tower carried State Police radio equipment for years is not supported by any source read: the Warren County document shows the summit as a county transmitter/receiver site but does not say State Police use the Gore site. The record's note that hikers still visit the site is also unsupported; the Register says the tower is closed to visitors, so the story does not say hikers visit. Wikipedia says the 1918 replacement was made by the Civilian Conservation Corps, which was not founded until 1933, so that claim is not used. The record's height_m 5.5 is the 1909 wooden tower (see corrections). The FLO New York list places the tower at -74.04878, about 3.6 km west of the Register and record coordinates (-74.00397), which match the Register's coordinates; the record coordinates were left as they are. No photos added: the Register's June 26, 2020 photo is credited to Laurie Rankin but its licence is not stated.
